verificationMethods.description: Inspection of specifications, schemas, generated artifacts, or source boundaries
Contract test against public input or output behavior
Fault injection, crash recovery, or concurrency test

gates.exitCondition: Inputs, outcomes, evidence policy, boundaries, and prohibited claims are mechanically defined.
The system can make exact, snapshot-bound, evidence-bearing read claims without false completeness.
Every supported invocation has exact semantic mappings or a precise unsupported outcome.
Value-propagation claims have distinct meanings, bounded witnesses, and sound negative-proof rules.
A target condition can be converted into a deterministic, obligation-complete plan without source mutation.
A valid plan can be applied within exact authority, identity, generation, content, and write boundaries.
The changed repository is re-evaluated and the target condition is mechanically proven or rejected.
The accepted behavior remains correct under enterprise scale, failure, concurrency, tampering, and operational diagnosis.
One repository-wide transformation satisfies the full specification.

requirements.requirement: Requirement identifiers MUST be permanent.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A retired or superseded identifier remains reserved and is not assigned to another requirement.

requirements.requirement: Each requirement MUST describe one independently verifiable obligation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Every row has a specific observable pass or fail condition.

requirements.requirement: Every implemented requirement MUST reference its executable or inspectable evidence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A requirement-to-evidence ledger identifies the command, test, artifact, or inspection result.

requirements.requirement: Documentation alone MUST NOT satisfy a behavioral requirement.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Behavioral requirements reference executable evidence.

requirements.requirement: A requirement MUST NOT be marked complete when its prerequisite requirements are incomplete.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The requirement ledger rejects invalid completion states.

requirements.requirement: Every semantic operation MUST bind to one canonical repository root.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A request using a different root, alias, worktree, or escaped path is rejected or resolved to the same canonical root before analysis.

requirements.requirement: Semantic identity MUST originate from compiler analysis.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Same-named but unrelated declarations remain distinct, and overloads are not selected by text order.

requirements.requirement: Semantic relationships MUST retain their source occurrence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Every relationship includes its source file and exact source range.

requirements.requirement: Compiler-derived evidence MUST remain queryable after the producing analysis request ends.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A later read against the same semantic state returns equivalent evidence without reconstructing identity from text.

requirements.requirement: Every semantic read MUST bind to one semantic generation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Generation movement during a read causes restart or rejection, never a mixed result.

requirements.requirement: Every result MUST expose its evidence limitations.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Excluded, limited, failed, stale, pending, unsupported, and truncated evidence are visible and distinct.

requirements.requirement: Missing evidence MUST NOT be converted into semantic absence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Incomplete evidence returns qualification or rejection rather than an exact zero or absence claim.

requirements.requirement: Source mutation MUST require explicit authority bound to the exact repository state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Stale, tampered, wrong-root, and wrong-generation mutation attempts are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Every operation MUST identify one repository state, one scope, one source condition, one target condition, one boundary set, and one evidence policy where those inputs are applicable.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Admission fails when a required input cannot be established.

requirements.requirement: Every operation MUST produce exactly one semantic outcome: complete, qualified, or rejected.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The public result contract excludes overlapping or undefined outcome states.

requirements.requirement: A complete outcome MUST include proof that all required target conditions hold over the admitted scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Removing any required proof element invalidates the result.

requirements.requirement: A qualified outcome MUST be structurally impossible to interpret as complete.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Qualification is encoded in the canonical result state, not only in prose.

requirements.requirement: A rejected outcome MUST identify the exact failed requirement and whether mutation occurred.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Rejection output includes requirement identity, affected scope, evidence inspected, and mutation state.

requirements.requirement: The default evidence policy MUST fail closed.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Omitting evidence-policy input never enables partial mutation, unsupported absence, or inferred completeness.

requirements.requirement: Compilation success, test success, or absence of text matches MUST NOT independently establish transformation completion.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A deliberately incomplete semantic transformation that compiles remains incomplete.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT represent a partial semantic transformation as complete.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Fault injection between stages cannot produce a complete result.

requirements.requirement: Repository input MUST identify the canonical repository root.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Relative, aliased, symlinked, and worktree paths resolve to a single admitted root or fail.

requirements.requirement: Repository input MUST identify the exact source state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Revision, tracked changes, admitted untracked files, and generated inputs are represented or explicitly excluded.

requirements.requirement: Repository input MUST identify all build and compiler inputs that can change semantic resolution.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Changing compiler version, language settings, dependencies, source sets, variants, or compiler plugins changes repository-state identity.

requirements.requirement: Scope input MUST be mechanically resolvable.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unknown or ambiguous modules, source sets, declarations, or families are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Build ownership MUST outrank directory inference when build metadata is available.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A misleading directory layout does not alter module or source-set scope.

requirements.requirement: The source condition MUST be mechanically evaluable before it can authorize mutation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Natural-language input alone cannot pass mutation admission.

requirements.requirement: The target condition MUST be mechanically evaluable before planning completes.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A target described only by subjective quality, intention, or prose is rejected.

requirements.requirement: Boundary input MUST identify each accepted boundary and the claims permitted at that boundary.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A boundary lacking scope or claim semantics is rejected.

requirements.requirement: Evidence-policy input MUST define the treatment of incomplete evidence, negative claims, tests, generated sources, and qualified mutation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unsupported or contradictory policy combinations are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Resource bounds MUST be established before unbounded analysis begins.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Missing required bounds produce admission failure or server-owned defaults visible in the result.

requirements.requirement: Contradictory inputs MUST be rejected before source mutation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Mutually exclusive source conditions, target conditions, boundaries, or policies produce a typed rejection.

requirements.requirement: The requested scope MUST reduce to one coherent semantic configuration.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A scope requiring incompatible compiler or dependency states is split explicitly or rejected.

requirements.requirement: Each semantic snapshot MUST bind the canonical root, source state, compiler configuration, dependency resolution, build ownership, and semantic generation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Changing any bound input produces a distinct snapshot identity.

requirements.requirement: Reasoning against a snapshot MUST observe immutable semantic evidence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Concurrent publication of a newer generation does not alter an active read.

requirements.requirement: A result MUST NOT combine coverage from one snapshot with semantic evidence from another.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Forced generation movement produces restart or rejection.

requirements.requirement: Snapshot completeness MUST be measured against an expected inventory.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Indexing every discovered file is insufficient when expected files remain absent.

requirements.requirement: The expected inventory MUST derive from admitted build and source ownership.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unowned directory enumeration cannot establish complete compilation scope.

requirements.requirement: Snapshot state MUST distinguish included, excluded, failed, stale, pending, removed, and unsupported inputs.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Each state can be independently induced and observed.

requirements.requirement: Snapshot admissibility MUST be claim-specific.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A snapshot admitted for exact identity may still be rejected for repository-wide absence.

requirements.requirement: Source movement after snapshot creation MUST invalidate affected claims.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A content or configuration change cannot reuse stale proof.

requirements.requirement: Concurrent readers MUST observe coherent snapshots.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Parallel reads return internally consistent generations and coverage.

requirements.requirement: Concurrent semantic writers MUST NOT publish mixed or partially committed generations.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Forced writer failure leaves either the prior valid generation or one complete new generation.

requirements.requirement: Only the admitted semantic authority MAY publish compiler-grounded repository evidence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A second process or guessed storage path cannot become an accepted writer.

requirements.requirement: Snapshot identity MUST remain distinguishable across worktrees and repository roots.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Identical revisions in separate worktrees do not share mutable authority or continuation state.

requirements.requirement: Every supported declaration MUST have compiler-grounded identity sufficient to distinguish it from every other admitted declaration.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Identity tests cover overloads, members, extensions, locals, constructors, accessors, and source sets.

requirements.requirement: Display name, fully qualified name, source text, path, offset, or textual signature MUST NOT independently replace exact identity.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Collision fixtures cannot cause silent identity merging.

requirements.requirement: Discovery output MUST contain a value accepted directly by downstream exact operations.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Every returned candidate round-trips through exact selection without caller reconstruction.

requirements.requirement: Exact identity MUST survive every downstream read operation without loss of discrimination.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A selected overload remains the same overload through relationship, propagation, and planning requests.

requirements.requirement: A stale identity MUST be rejected after any semantic change that invalidates it.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Moving, replacing, or changing a declaration causes prior identity use to fail or re-resolve explicitly.

requirements.requirement: Semantic family membership MUST be established explicitly.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Override, implementation, inheritance, expect/actual, sealed, delegated, and synthetic membership cannot be inferred from names.

requirements.requirement: Family completeness MUST be reported separately from individual identity resolution.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: One resolved member does not imply a complete family.

requirements.requirement: Synthetic and generated declarations MUST remain distinguishable from authored declarations.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Result data and scope policies can select or exclude each category.

requirements.requirement: Identity projection for human display MUST NOT become a selectable authority unless explicitly round-trippable.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Editing a display label cannot alter selected semantic identity.

requirements.requirement: Every semantic claim MUST identify its evidence source and snapshot.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Claims lacking provenance are rejected by output validation.

requirements.requirement: Every relationship MUST identify source identity, target identity, occurrence location, relationship meaning, and compiler basis.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Required fields are present and internally coherent.

requirements.requirement: Any redirection, lifting, grouping, or projection of compiler evidence MUST be explicitly recorded.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Projected endpoints cannot appear as direct compiler relationships.

requirements.requirement: Persisted compiler evidence MUST remain distinguishable from lexical, inferred, generated, user-provided, and model-generated information.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Query output identifies the evidence class for every contributing source.

requirements.requirement: Every result MUST include the coverage required to interpret that result.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Empty, non-empty, qualified, and rejected outcomes carry coverage data.

requirements.requirement: Coverage MUST identify expected, admitted, indexed, excluded, failed, stale, pending, and unsupported scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Each category is represented independently.

requirements.requirement: Coverage MUST state whether positive claims, negative claims, or both are supported.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Incomplete evidence cannot accidentally support absence.

requirements.requirement: A confidence value MUST NOT substitute for structured coverage.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Removing structured coverage invalidates the result even when confidence remains high.

requirements.requirement: Truncation and continuation state MUST be explicit.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Result size limits never appear as terminal completeness.

requirements.requirement: An empty result under incomplete evidence MUST remain distinct from proven absence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Fixtures produce separate complete-empty and qualified-empty outcomes.

requirements.requirement: A rejected proof MUST retain the evidence envelope explaining rejection.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Rejection includes generation, requested scope, relevant coverage, and failed predicate.

requirements.requirement: Every limitation MUST identify its reason and affected scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A generic limitation without affected files, source sets, relationship families, or boundaries is insufficient when that information exists.

requirements.requirement: Every recoverable limitation MUST identify only actions capable of changing the failed predicate.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Suggested recovery is tested to alter the stated evidence condition or is omitted.

requirements.requirement: Continuation state MUST bind the repository root, snapshot, scope, normalized request, ordering, and resume position.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Reuse after changing any bound input is rejected.

requirements.requirement: Complete negative proof MUST require complete relevant coverage, terminal traversal, and no undeclared boundary.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Removing any prerequisite converts absence to qualification or rejection.

requirements.requirement: Every supported invocation MUST identify the exact invoked declaration.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Overloaded, inherited, extension, constructor, operator, and delegated calls resolve without name-based guessing.

requirements.requirement: Every supported invocation MUST identify its exact source occurrence and nearest admitted owner.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Invocation evidence includes repository-relative location and owning semantic identity.

requirements.requirement: Every supported invocation MUST identify its dispatch receiver when one exists.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Explicit and implicit dispatch-receiver fixtures produce exact mappings.

requirements.requirement: Every supported invocation MUST identify its extension receiver when one exists.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Extension-call fixtures produce exact mappings distinct from dispatch receivers.

requirements.requirement: Every supported invocation MUST identify required context inputs when present.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Context-input fixtures preserve exact parameter and supplied-value identity.

requirements.requirement: Every explicit argument MUST map to the exact parameter it satisfies.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Positional and named arguments remain correct under reordered declarations and overloads.

requirements.requirement: Defaulted, implicit, and omitted arguments MUST remain distinguishable from explicitly supplied arguments.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Invocation output records the source of every satisfied parameter.

requirements.requirement: Variable-arity arguments and trailing lambdas MUST retain their exact parameter mapping and order.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Multiple arguments mapped to one parameter remain individually identifiable.

requirements.requirement: Inferred type substitutions relevant to invocation semantics MUST be retained.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Generic-call fixtures expose actual substitutions rather than declaration-level type parameters only.

requirements.requirement: Compiler-inserted conversions relevant to a declared condition MUST remain visible.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A target condition sensitive to conversion cannot be evaluated from pre-conversion type alone.

requirements.requirement: Invocation results MUST identify the resulting semantic value or explicitly state why no value exists.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Functions, constructors, property accesses, assignments, and `Unit`-like outcomes are distinct.

requirements.requirement: Read, write, compound-access, suspension, and throwable behavior required by a declared condition MUST be represented or explicitly unsupported.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Relevant fixtures cannot collapse these meanings into a generic call.

requirements.requirement: Callable references MUST remain distinct from actual invocation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Referencing a callable does not create an invocation edge or argument mapping.

requirements.requirement: Unsupported or unresolved invocation semantics MUST identify the exact unsupported portion.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A partially resolved call cannot be represented as fully exact.

requirements.requirement: No invocation may be classified as exact when a required receiver, parameter, type substitution, or target mapping is unresolved.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Deliberately incomplete fixtures produce qualification or rejection.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST account for values entering through parameters, receivers, context inputs, captures, properties, external inputs, and admitted boundaries.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Each ingress form participates in a propagation query.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST account for assignments, aliases, destructuring, casts, conversions, wrapping, extraction, and intermediate expressions relevant to the declared condition.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Fixtures preserve value identity through each supported event.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST account for branches, conditional expressions, loops, jumps, and early exits relevant to the declared claim.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Path-sensitive fixtures distinguish feasible and infeasible propagation.

requirements.requirement: Propagation across callable boundaries MUST use exact invocation mappings.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Argument-to-parameter and return-to-recipient transitions are linked to INV evidence.

requirements.requirement: Return values, thrown values, property writes, and externally visible effects MUST remain distinct.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A returned value cannot be confused with a stored, logged, thrown, or transmitted value.

requirements.requirement: Every propagation claim MUST have one explicit meaning: exact binding, required propagation, possible propagation, proven absence, incomplete evidence, accepted boundary, unsupported behavior, or stale evidence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The canonical output contract prevents meaning overlap.

requirements.requirement: Different propagation meanings MUST NOT be collapsed into one generic relationship.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The same endpoints may have separate claims with different meanings.

requirements.requirement: Every positive propagation claim MUST provide a bounded witness or a bounded reference to one.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A caller can inspect the semantic steps supporting the claim.

requirements.requirement: A witness MUST identify relevant intermediate events, invocation boundaries, conditions, conversions, and accepted boundaries.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Removing a required witness step invalidates the claim.

requirements.requirement: A required-propagation claim MUST establish that every admitted execution path satisfies the relationship.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A fixture with one bypass path cannot produce a required-propagation result.

requirements.requirement: A possible-propagation claim MUST establish at least one admitted feasible path.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Syntactically present but semantically infeasible paths do not qualify.

requirements.requirement: Proven absence MUST satisfy EVD-015 and complete all relevant propagation analysis.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Introducing one stale file, unsupported event, truncated path, or undeclared boundary invalidates absence.

requirements.requirement: Cycles and recursion MUST terminate deterministically without semantic duplication.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Repeated analysis of cyclic fixtures returns equivalent bounded results.

requirements.requirement: Exceeding a propagation bound MUST produce qualification or rejection, never silent completeness.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Depth, path, time, and memory limits are independently tested.

requirements.requirement: Static propagation claims MUST NOT be presented as runtime certainty beyond their declared boundary.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Reflection, dynamic loading, mutable external state, and framework indirection remain explicit.

requirements.requirement: Planning MUST begin from admitted source and target semantic conditions.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: No plan can be created from source text replacement alone.

requirements.requirement: Text search, regular expressions, embeddings, labels, and model output MUST NOT independently determine affected semantic scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Deliberate text collisions do not expand or contract the semantic plan.

requirements.requirement: The plan MUST identify all semantic identities whose contract, behavior, or representation must change to satisfy the target condition.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Omitting one required declaration, caller, implementation, or boundary makes planning incomplete.

requirements.requirement: Unknown affected scope MUST block a complete plan.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Incomplete family, invocation, propagation, or boundary evidence prevents complete admission.

requirements.requirement: The plan MUST declare all required preconditions.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Preconditions include identity, family, invocation, propagation, coverage, boundary, freshness, authority, and resource requirements where relevant.

requirements.requirement: Source mutation MUST NOT begin before every mandatory precondition passes.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Mutation entry points reject plans with one unsatisfied precondition.

requirements.requirement: The plan MUST produce a finite set of uniquely identifiable obligations.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Every required semantic change or proof condition has one stable obligation entry.

requirements.requirement: Every obligation MUST identify its scope, evidence basis, required result, and completion rule.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: An obligation lacking any required field fails validation.

requirements.requirement: Every planned source change MUST link to at least one obligation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unmotivated source changes are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Every obligation MUST survive planning, mutation, and verification until discharged or explicitly failed.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Obligation count and identity reconcile across all stages.

requirements.requirement: The intended semantic result MUST be calculated before source mutation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The plan includes expected additions, removals, contract changes, invocation changes, propagation changes, boundaries, files, and diagnostics where relevant.

requirements.requirement: A plan MUST be rejected when its intended semantic result cannot satisfy the target condition.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: An internally contradictory or insufficient plan never reaches mutation admission.

requirements.requirement: Equivalent inputs against the same snapshot MUST produce equivalent plans.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Repeated and shuffled-input replays produce the same affected scope, obligations, stages, and ordering.

requirements.requirement: Plan ordering MUST be deterministic.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Source enumeration, database row order, thread scheduling, and discovery order do not alter the canonical plan.

requirements.requirement: A multi-stage plan MUST define explicit preconditions, semantic delta, obligations, and completion criteria for each stage.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: No stage exists only as an execution convenience without semantic meaning.

requirements.requirement: Each intermediate stage MUST satisfy its declared validity policy.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A stage declared compilable, diagnosable, or proof-preserving is verified accordingly.

requirements.requirement: A stage MUST NOT weaken the final target condition or silently remove obligations.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Stage composition yields the original final obligation set.

requirements.requirement: The plan MUST exclude unrelated cleanup, refactoring, formatting, dependency changes, and documentation changes unless required by an obligation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Diff inspection finds no change without obligation linkage.

requirements.requirement: Mutation authority MUST bind the canonical root, repository state, semantic generation, active runtime, requester, write scope, and protocol state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Changing any bound value invalidates authority.

requirements.requirement: Tampered, stale, wrong-root, wrong-runtime, wrong-requester, or wrong-generation authority MUST be rejected.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Each invalid state produces a distinct rejection.

requirements.requirement: Mutation MUST operate through exact semantic identity and current source location.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Same-named unrelated source remains unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Source content freshness MUST be verified immediately before applying each affected change or atomic change group.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Concurrent source modification causes conflict rather than overwrite.

requirements.requirement: Every write MUST remain inside the canonical repository root and declared write scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Traversal, symlink, absolute-path, and worktree-escape attempts are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Conflicting, overlapping, stale, or semantically inconsistent edits MUST be rejected.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Conflict fixtures do not produce best-effort partial application.

requirements.requirement: Qualified evidence MUST NOT authorize mutation unless the evidence policy explicitly permits the exact qualified operation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Default policy rejects mutation under incomplete required evidence.

requirements.requirement: Every applied change MUST record file, source range, prior content identity, resulting content identity, and motivating obligation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Mutation receipt reconciles exactly with the diff.

requirements.requirement: Mutation output MUST be deterministic for equivalent plan and repository inputs.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Replay produces equivalent applied changes and canonical receipt.

requirements.requirement: A failed atomic mutation MUST leave the prior source state intact.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Fault injection at each write boundary restores or preserves the original state.

requirements.requirement: A failed staged mutation that cannot roll back MUST produce an explicit incomplete-repository state that cannot be interpreted as success.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Process failure between stages is visible in durable state and result output.

requirements.requirement: Mutation MUST NOT apply changes unrelated to a declared obligation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Every changed range has an obligation reference; extra changes fail verification.

requirements.requirement: Each stage MUST bind to one semantic generation and exact source state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Repository movement between stages requires re-admission.

requirements.requirement: Mutation completion MUST NOT imply transformation completion.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Successful application returns an awaiting-verification state until G6 passes.

requirements.requirement: The changed repository MUST be treated as untrusted until compiler-grounded re-evaluation completes.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Mutation completion cannot directly emit final success.

requirements.requirement: A successful source mutation MUST produce or admit a new semantic generation before final proof.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Final proof cannot reference only the source generation.

requirements.requirement: Changed and affected semantic identities MUST be resolved again against the resulting repository state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Planned identities are compared with observed identities.

requirements.requirement: Relevant relationships, invocation mappings, propagation claims, and coverage MUST be recomputed or soundly reused under the resulting generation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Reuse requires unchanged bound inputs and invalidation proof.

requirements.requirement: Required compiler diagnostics MUST be evaluated under the resulting repository state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Diagnostic policy is applied after semantic refresh, not before mutation only.

requirements.requirement: Every obligation MUST be evaluated against the resulting state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Each obligation reaches discharged or failed; none remain implicit.

requirements.requirement: Every target condition MUST be evaluated against the resulting state and admitted scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Target proof references the final generation and final coverage.

requirements.requirement: Every required source-condition removal MUST be evaluated independently.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A target addition cannot hide continued existence of the prohibited source state.

requirements.requirement: The intended semantic result MUST be compared with the observed semantic result.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Additions, removals, changed contracts, calls, propagation, boundaries, and diagnostics reconcile.

requirements.requirement: Every unexpected semantic difference MUST be explained, explicitly accepted by policy, or cause failure.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: No unexpected difference is silently discarded.

requirements.requirement: Completion MUST require all mandatory obligations, target conditions, source removals, coverage conditions, and diagnostic conditions to pass.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Removing any mandatory proof item changes success to failure.

requirements.requirement: Final proof MUST bind the final canonical root, source state, compiler state, dependency state, scope, and semantic generation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Replaying proof against a changed input fails.

requirements.requirement: Final proof MUST contain enough information to re-evaluate the same claims against the same repository state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A clean replay reproduces equivalent proof.

requirements.requirement: Compilation or tests MAY be required by evidence policy, but MUST remain separate from semantic proof.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The result identifies compiler, test, and semantic evidence independently.

requirements.requirement: A final unstable or moved repository state MUST invalidate completion.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Source movement during final proof causes restart or rejection.

requirements.requirement: Every canonical result MUST be machine-readable.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Complete, qualified, and rejected outcomes validate against a closed result contract.

requirements.requirement: Human-readable output MUST derive from the canonical result rather than independently reinterpret behavior.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Equivalent canonical data produces equivalent semantic status in human output.

requirements.requirement: Every result MUST identify repository state, semantic generation, scope, evidence policy, boundaries, coverage, limits, truncation, schema version, and result identity.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Required envelope fields exist for all outcome categories.

requirements.requirement: Analysis output MUST identify selected identities, ambiguity, relationships, invocation mappings, propagation meanings, witnesses, and limitations where applicable.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Omitted required analysis fields invalidate the result.

requirements.requirement: Plan output MUST identify source condition, target condition, affected scope, obligations, expected semantic result, stages, preconditions, verification rules, and plan identity.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The plan is independently inspectable before mutation.

requirements.requirement: Mutation output MUST identify source and resulting state, applied changes, obligation linkage, conflicts, rollback state, and mutation identity.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The receipt reconciles with repository changes.

requirements.requirement: Completion output MUST identify final target evaluation, source-condition removal, discharged obligations, final coverage, diagnostics, semantic differences, boundaries, and proof identity.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Completion cannot be represented without each required category.

requirements.requirement: Rejection output MUST identify failed requirement, failure category, affected scope, inspected evidence, missing evidence, mutation state, recoverability, and failure identity.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Every rejection fixture contains the required data.

requirements.requirement: Qualified output MUST encode qualification in the result type and every projection.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Filtering human output cannot turn a qualified canonical result into success.

requirements.requirement: Process status, protocol status, and human status MUST agree on semantic success or failure.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A semantic rejection cannot exit as unattended shell success.

requirements.requirement: Equivalent inputs against the same state MUST produce equivalent canonical results, excluding declared operational metadata.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Replay produces stable ordering and result identity.

requirements.requirement: Output MUST NOT expose unrelated credentials, secrets, private environment values, or signing material.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Sanitization and adversarial fixtures show no leakage.

requirements.requirement: Failures MUST be typed by semantic meaning.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Invalid input, repository movement, incomplete evidence, planning failure, mutation failure, and proof failure remain distinct.

requirements.requirement: A failure MUST identify the exact requirement or admission predicate that failed.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Generic “failed” or “incomplete” output is rejected when a precise predicate exists.

requirements.requirement: A failure MUST identify the exact affected scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: File, source set, module, family, relationship category, or boundary scope is included where known.

requirements.requirement: A failure MUST state whether source mutation began and whether rollback completed.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Mutation and non-mutation failures are unambiguous.

requirements.requirement: Recoverability MUST be explicit.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The result identifies whether retry, refresh, scope change, boundary declaration, source correction, or no supported action applies.

requirements.requirement: Resource-bound exhaustion MUST remain distinct from semantic absence or unsupported behavior.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Time, memory, depth, result, and path exhaustion have separate outcomes.

requirements.requirement: Transport success MUST NOT imply semantic success.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A valid protocol exchange containing rejection produces semantic failure status.

requirements.requirement: Rollback failure MUST be distinct from operation failure with successful rollback.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Fault injection produces separate durable states.

requirements.requirement: Every failure MUST have stable machine-readable identity.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Equivalent deterministic failures produce equivalent failure classification and identity.

requirements.requirement: A failure MUST NOT claim a recovery action can change the result unless that action addresses the failed predicate.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Recovery-action tests validate predicate relevance.

requirements.requirement: Kotlin compiler analysis MUST remain the authority for Kotlin identity, resolution, type, and compiler relationship claims.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: No lexical or model-derived result can satisfy those claims.

requirements.requirement: Non-Kotlin evidence MUST identify its separate authority and certainty.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Documentation, schema, build, workflow, and other-language evidence cannot appear as Kotlin compiler proof.

requirements.requirement: Gradle metadata MUST remain the authority for build, module, variant, and source-set ownership where available.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Directory layout cannot override admitted Gradle ownership.

requirements.requirement: External implementation behavior MUST NOT be claimed without admitted source or a separately declared evidence source.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: External calls terminate or qualify behavior claims as required.

requirements.requirement: Static evidence MUST NOT be presented as proof of runtime behavior dependent on reflection, dynamic loading, mutable external state, concurrency, timing, environment, network, database, native code, or runtime proxies.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Each runtime-sensitive fixture produces an explicit boundary.

requirements.requirement: A language model MAY assist discovery, translation, explanation, or source rendering, but MUST NOT establish semantic identity, completeness, absence, propagation, or completion.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Removing model output does not change canonical proof; injecting incorrect model output cannot create proof.

requirements.requirement: Text search, regular expressions, labels, embeddings, and documentation MAY assist retrieval but MUST NOT create semantic evidence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Retrieval-only inputs cannot create identities or relationships absent from compiler evidence.

requirements.requirement: An undeclared boundary affecting a required claim MUST cause qualification or rejection.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A hidden reflective or external boundary prevents complete proof.

requirements.requirement: Every accepted boundary MUST state which positive and negative claims may cross or terminate at it.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Boundary input lacking claim semantics is rejected.

requirements.requirement: Persisted storage MUST NOT become an independent semantic authority detached from compiler provenance.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Corrupted or provenance-free stored evidence is rejected.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST publish supported scale targets for repository size, module count, source count, relationship count, and concurrent readers.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Versioned benchmark profiles define accepted limits.

requirements.requirement: A local source change SHOULD invalidate only evidence that can no longer be trusted.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Incremental benchmarks show bounded invalidation while soundness tests prevent under-invalidation.

requirements.requirement: Output bounds MUST also bound or expose underlying work.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A small result limit cannot hide uncontrolled full-repository work without reporting it.

requirements.requirement: Large result ordering MUST be deterministic.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Repeated parallel executions return the same canonical order.

requirements.requirement: Pagination or continuation MUST preserve root, snapshot, scope, filters, ordering, evidence policy, and resume position.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Changed state or request invalidates continuation.

requirements.requirement: Durable progress MUST survive process failure without publishing a partial snapshot as complete.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Crash injection after each bounded work unit resumes from committed progress.

requirements.requirement: A failed writer MUST NOT corrupt or remove the prior valid snapshot.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Prior generation remains readable after forced failure.

requirements.requirement: Concurrent readers MUST not block or observe partially committed semantic evidence beyond declared database behavior.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Load tests retain coherent snapshots under writer activity.

requirements.requirement: Concurrent writers MUST be serialized, isolated, or rejected so that one semantic authority remains.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Competing writers cannot both publish conflicting state.

requirements.requirement: Storage optimization MUST NOT weaken identity, provenance, occurrence location, or coverage.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Optimized and reference representations produce equivalent canonical evidence.

requirements.requirement: Exceeding a scale limit MUST produce a typed bounded outcome.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Resource exhaustion never causes silent truncation, false absence, or false completion.

requirements.requirement: Performance acceptance MUST measure both latency and agent-facing output cost.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Benchmarks record execution time, work performed, result bytes, page count, and canonical record count.

requirements.requirement: Only admitted local authority MAY produce or mutate compiler-grounded evidence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unadmitted processes and alternate paths are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Identity, continuation, plan, mutation authority, snapshot, result, and proof references MUST be tamper-evident.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Single-byte alteration causes rejection with a tamper-specific outcome.

requirements.requirement: Every read and write path MUST be normalized, contained, and independently verified.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Traversal, symlink, encoded path, case, and worktree escape fixtures fail.

requirements.requirement: External command execution MUST declare command, arguments, working directory, environment policy, bounds, expected outcome, and obligation linkage.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Undeclared or unbounded execution is rejected.

requirements.requirement: External command exit status and captured output MUST be retained as evidence without becoming semantic proof by themselves.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Build and test evidence remain separately classified.

requirements.requirement: Secrets and unrelated private values MUST be excluded from results, logs, persisted evidence, and proof artifacts.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Secret-seeded fixtures do not leak through normal or failure output.

requirements.requirement: Remote writes MUST require separate explicit authority.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Local mutation permission cannot authorize GitHub, artifact, registry, or other remote writes.

requirements.requirement: Requester and process identity reuse MUST NOT authorize a stale mutation session.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Process-ID reuse and replaced-runtime fixtures are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Runtime readiness, compiler readiness, inventory readiness, relationship readiness, propagation readiness, and mutation readiness MUST remain separate states.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: One ready capability cannot imply another.

requirements.requirement: Operational status MUST expose semantic generation and expected, indexed, excluded, failed, stale, pending, and unsupported counts.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Status reconciles with the canonical snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Active planning, mutation, and verification MUST expose current stage and obligation progress.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: An interrupted operation can identify completed, active, and remaining obligations.

requirements.requirement: A blocked operation MUST expose the exact failed predicate and affected scope.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Generic readiness failure is insufficient when precise evidence exists.

requirements.requirement: Resource use and configured bounds MUST be observable.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Time, memory, path, depth, page, and result consumption are reported where relevant.

requirements.requirement: Limitation output MUST support prioritizing recovery without weakening fail-closed behavior.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Scope and reason are visible without returning unsupported semantic claims.

requirements.requirement: A compact status projection MUST NOT discard capability distinctions required for safe automation.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Automation can determine whether a requested operation is admissible without interpreting prose.

requirements.requirement: Diagnostic output MUST distinguish incorrect behavior from intentional rejection caused by an unmet invariant.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Fault fixtures and incomplete-evidence fixtures produce different classifications.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT claim proof of arbitrary runtime behavior.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Runtime-dependent fixtures terminate at explicit boundaries.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT claim to solve undecidable program properties.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unsupported target conditions are rejected rather than approximated as proof.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT infer undeclared business meaning as semantic fact.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Domain labels or model interpretation cannot establish a target condition.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT replace tests, runtime telemetry, or external validation when the evidence policy requires them.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Semantic proof reports required external evidence separately.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT claim support for a language, compiler plugin, build mode, or semantic construct that it cannot analyze soundly.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unsupported configurations produce explicit admission failure.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT preserve binary, source, serialization, or behavioral compatibility unless the target condition or evidence policy requires it.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Compatibility is an explicit obligation, never an implied promise.

requirements.requirement: The system MUST NOT autonomously accept an unknown boundary.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Unknown boundaries require declared policy or cause qualification or rejection.

requirements.requirement: A heuristic score MUST NOT substitute for exact evidence or proof.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: High-ranked or high-confidence heuristic output cannot authorize completion.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST operate across multiple Gradle-owned modules or source sets.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The admitted scope crosses at least two build ownership boundaries.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST define exact source and target conditions.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Both conditions are machine-readable and independently evaluable.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST include multiple declaration families and invocation forms.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Overloads, implementations or overrides, direct calls, and at least one non-trivial invocation form are present.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST use exact parameter, receiver, and argument mappings.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Every changed invocation links to the exact changed callable contract.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST evaluate value propagation across callable boundaries.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: At least one target condition depends on interprocedural propagation.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST contain at least one external, reflective, generated, or otherwise dynamic boundary.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The boundary is declared and affects proof interpretation.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST apply source changes in one or more semantically defined stages.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Each stage has preconditions, obligations, expected semantic result, and verification.

requirements.requirement: The resulting repository MUST be re-evaluated from compiler-grounded evidence.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Final proof references the resulting semantic generation.

requirements.requirement: The demonstration MUST prove the target condition and any required removal of the source condition.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Both proofs are independently present.

requirements.requirement: Same-named but semantically unrelated code MUST remain unchanged.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Text-collision fixtures are included in the repository.

requirements.requirement: Overloads MUST remain distinct throughout discovery, planning, mutation, and proof.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Only the admitted overload and its exact dependents change.

requirements.requirement: No required caller, implementation, or boundary MAY be silently omitted.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Deliberately removing one required evidence record prevents completion.

requirements.requirement: Unsupported callers or boundaries MUST remain explicit.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: An unsupported path produces qualification or rejection rather than completion.

requirements.requirement: The final plan and proof MUST be reproducible against the same repository state.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: A clean replay produces equivalent canonical plan and proof identities.

requirements.requirement: Given one admitted repository state, one declared source condition, one declared target condition, one declared scope, one declared boundary set, and one declared evidence policy, the system MUST either produce and apply a deterministic sequence of compiler-valid source changes and prove that the target condition holds over that scope, or return the exact evidence boundary that prevents proof.
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: DEM-001 through DEM-014 pass as one end-to-end acceptance suite. No partial, qualified, stale, truncated, ambiguous, unsupported, or unverified outcome can be represented as complete.
